summary: At 14:00–14:02Z auth-service error rate stepped from ~0.2% to a flat ~36% and stayed there for ~2h, with one upstream api-gateway 5xx step (~21%), no load/latency/resource change in auth-service, and no co-degradation of any other service. The change set bracketing onset is exactly two auth-service changes one minute apart: deploy dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, jjwt 0.12 parser + TokenValidator rewrite) at 14:00:00Z and config cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) at 14:01:00Z. H1 (bad deployment, 0.40) and H2 (signing-key rotation, 0.40) are both well-grounded, both co-located with the 2-minute-resolution onset, name different origins with different fixes, and each rests on one unverified pivotal hop ('parser rejects a subset' vs 'old key no longer resolves') that no available tool can test — no per-kid/audience/per-replica metric exists, auth-service logs are 503, and no JWKS/key-store publish state or TTL/grace config is retrievable. H3 (shared redis-cache) and H4 (client-side) are contradicted by verified telemetry, and api-gateway is ruled out as the origin. Outcome is therefore inconclusive, with the trigger firmly localized to one of auth-service's two changes but not separable from retrievable data.

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service v7.3.0 (jjwt 0.12 parser rewrite) rejects a subset of otherwise-valid tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 14:00Z deploy dep-5710 of auth-service v7.3.0 rewrote TokenValidator and moved from jjwt 0.11 to the breaking 0.12 parser API. The new parser behaves differently on a class of tokens (stricter claim/header parsing, changed clock-skew default as in HIST-109), so ~36% of validations return invalid_token immediately while the rest pass. Nothing was rolled back, so the step persists flat for 2h.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 deploys auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z with 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten', status live, not rolled back
The rewritten parser rejects a subset of otherwise-valid tokens as invalid_token (mechanism assumed; a uniform parser break would give ~100%, not ~36%)
auth-service error_rate steps instantly from 0.21% (14:00Z bucket) through 18.12% (14:01Z bucket) to 37.28% (14:03Z bucket) and stays flat ~36% for ~2h
Failures are returned fast, not timed out: request_rate flat ~395-410 req/s, p99 ~87-92ms, CPU ~38%, memory ~52%, rate-limited ~2/min, pod restarts 0
api-gateway, auth's only caller, steps to ~21% sustained 5xx in the matching bucket; other gateway downstreams (order-service) stay flat, so the fault is confined to auth-calling traffic

assumptions: The rewritten TokenValidator/jjwt 0.12 parser rejects only a subset of tokens rather than all (unverified; no per-token-class metric exists — F30)
The 'subset' is a class of tokens rather than a subset of replicas: pod-level version distribution is unavailable (F31) and restarts are 0 (F32), so partial rollout is neither shown nor excluded
cfg-2705 is service-scoped and fleet-wide (F19), which if anything argues the 36% subset is token-based rather than config-application-based

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2705 signing-key rotation (k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) leaves old-key tokens unvalidatable
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 at 14:01:00Z switched the active jwt.signing.key_id to k-2026-04. Tokens minted under k-2025-10 and still within TTL fail validation (old key no longer resolved / not published in a consumable JWKS), producing 401 invalid_token for the ~1/3 of validations carrying the old key, persisting flat because the mix of in-flight old-key tokens does not decay away within 2h or the old key stays unresolvable.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: auth-service (jwt signing key material / JWKS publication)

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 changes jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' -> 'k-2026-04' at 14:01:00Z by security-automation, scope auth-service, the only config change in a two-week lookback
The verification path no longer resolves the old key_id (old key unpublished / not loaded), so old-key tokens fail
error_rate begins stepping inside the 14:01Z bucket (avg 18.12%) and is fully established at ~37% by 14:03Z, one-two buckets after the rotation
Failures are immediate invalid_token, not timeouts — throughput, latency and resources are flat
Downstream api-gateway 5xx steps in the same bucket and stays ~21%, matching the auth-calling subset

assumptions: Old-key tokens in flight are ~1/3 of validation traffic (token TTL mix) — assumed, not measured; no TTL/overlap/grace config is queryable
The key store / JWKS is not itself fully broken (would give ~100% failure)
Whether k-2025-10 still resolves after 14:01Z is undetermined: no JWKS publish-state, key last-loaded timestamp or key-store node exists in the tool surface or dependency graph (F21, F22, F23)
No companion grace/overlap setting was changed (none exists in the config record — F20)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared redis-cache fault fails a subset of auth-service token/session validations
ranked_hypotheses.statement: redis-cache is the only shared component auth-service depends on (also used by portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service). A degradation at ~14:02Z (evictions, connection errors, or a platform-side change outside the queried windows) would make a subset of token/session lookups fail, surfacing as auth-service invalid_token 401s without load or latency change inside auth-service.

causal_chain.claim: auth-service depends on shared redis-cache (shared=true, owner platform), also used by portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service; redis-cache is the ONLY shared component in auth's direct dependency graph
redis-cache degrades at ~14:02Z (no change record and no error counter exist; only indirect health signals available)
Missed/failed cache lookups cause the token-validation step to return invalid_token for a subset
auth-service error_rate steps to ~36% with no internal resource or latency signal

assumptions: Token validation actually consults redis-cache on the failing path (not evidenced)
A redis-cache fault could be invisible to the deployment/config queries, which never covered redis-cache
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Now contradicted by verified telemetry rather than merely untested: redis-cache hit_ratio is flat/healthy 96.0-96.2% across onset (F25), connected_clients ~304-320 and evictions ~2.5-3.7/min unchanged with no step at 14:02Z (F26), and all three sibling consumers of redis-cache (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) stay flat at ~0.2% error rate through the window (F27, F28, F29). A shared-cache fault would co-degrade its other consumers. Also weakened by the fact that the failure is fast invalid_token rather than a lookup timeout (F12).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Client-side/artifact reading: stale client tokens or refresh issue, not an auth-side fault
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 36% figure is a partial view: only clients holding pre-change tokens (or a caller/audience subset) fail, so auth-service health is fine and the problem is client-side token refresh / clock skew; api-gateway's ~21% 5xx is the same subset seen one hop upstream.

causal_chain.claim: A subset of callers hold pre-change tokens and never refresh
auth-service returns invalid_token for exactly those requests, ~36% of validations
api-gateway shows a smaller (~21%) matching step because only its auth-calling traffic is affected

assumptions: The step would have to be explained with no auth-side cause, yet exactly two auth-side changes bracket onset
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: A client artifact cannot explain a flat ~36% step beginning inside the 14:01Z bucket, immediately after two auth-service changes (F13, F33), nor a matched 5xx step at auth's only caller while order-service (same gateway, no auth dependency) stays flat (F35). No per-caller breakdown exists to support a caller subset, and the two auth-side changes remain the only verified concurrent changes.

facts.statement: auth-service error_rate stepped from ~0.2% (14:00Z bucket avg 0.21%) to ~36-37% at 14:02Z, and at 2-minute resolution the step begins inside the 14:01:00Z bucket (avg 18.12%, max 36.08) and is fully established by 14:03Z (avg 37.28%).
The 36% error rate is a sustained flat step, ~36% in every 8-minute bucket from 14:08Z to 15:52Z with no recovery.

auth-service throughput and latency are unchanged across onset: request_rate flat ~395-410 req/s and latency_p99_ms ~87-92ms on both sides of 14:00Z, so 401s are returned quickly rather than timing out.
auth-service shows no resource saturation or rate limiting coincident with onset: cpu_pct ~37-39%, memory_pct ~51-53%, rate_limited_per_min ~2/min, and pod restarts flat at 0 across the window.

The complete change set bracketing onset is two auth-service changes one minute apart: dep-5710 auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z ('jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten', not rolled back) and cfg-2705 jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' -> 'k-2026-04' at 14:01:00Z by security-automation; no other deploys or config changes occurred in the window and nothing was rolled back after onset.
Timing cannot separate the two candidates: the last clean signal is 14:00Z, the deploy is 14:00:00Z, the key rotation is 14:01:00Z and onset is 14:02Z, which is within the 2-minute bucket resolution.

Across a two-week lookback for auth-service, cfg-2705 is the only config change recorded (count 1); there is no companion config entry for key store, JWKS publish, key TTL, overlap or grace period, and the change is recorded service-scoped, not per-pod.

api-gateway (auth-service's only caller) shows a simultaneous 5xx step from ~0.2% to a sustained ~21% with an onset bucket matching auth's, but it is not a shared component and had zero deployments and zero config changes since 2026-04-14T00:00Z, so it is ruled out as the origin of the change.
order-service, a sibling behind the same api-gateway, stays flat at ~0.21% error rate across 13:45Z-15:40Z, confining the gateway 5xx step to traffic that calls auth-service.

redis-cache (the only shared component in auth-service's dependency graph) is healthy across onset: hit_ratio_pct flat/healthy ~95.7-96.2%, connected_clients ~304-320 and evictions_per_min ~2.5-3.7 unchanged with no step at 14:02Z.

All three sibling consumers of redis-cache (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) stay flat at ~0.2% error rate from 13:45Z through ~15:59Z with no onset at 14:02Z, so co-degradation of a shared cache fault is absent and H3 is not supported.

auth-service exposes no per-endpoint, per-caller, per-issuer/audience or per-kid metric (only cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts), so the ~36% invalid_token cannot be attributed to a token class or caller.
No pod/instance-level or version/build label breakdown exists for auth-service, so a partial-rollout reading of the deploy cannot be tested from metrics.

No retrievable evidence can arbitrate H1 vs H2: there is no JWKS/key-store publish state, no key last-loaded/publish timestamp series, and no token TTL/overlap/grace configuration available, and the dependency graph contains no key-store/JWKS node (callers/callees are user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider).

Prior precedents cover both candidates: HIST-109 (auth library upgrade changed clock-skew default, fix: rollback + pinned skew config) mirrors dep-5710 and HIST-108 (401s after signing-key rotation; new key id published before all pods loaded the JWKS) mirrors cfg-2705; both are leads only and neither candidate is exonerated by history.

assumptions: Assumption: the rewritten TokenValidator / jjwt 0.12 parser rejects only a subset of tokens rather than all of them (H1's pivotal hop) — unverified, since no per-token-class metric exists (F30).

Assumption: the failing 'subset' is a class of tokens rather than a subset of replicas — pod-level version distribution is unavailable (F31) and restarts are 0 (F32), so partial rollout is neither shown nor excluded.

Assumption: old-key (k-2025-10) tokens still in flight are roughly one-third of validation traffic and that k-2025-10 no longer resolves after 14:01Z (H2's pivotal hop) — assumed, not measured; no TTL, overlap, grace config or JWKS publish state is retrievable (F20, F23).
Assumption: cfg-2705 applied atomically fleet-wide rather than per-instance with propagation lag — scope is only known at service granularity (F19).
Assumption: the ~1/3-vs-36% failure share 'matching a token-TTL population' is an unverified quantitative fit; no TTL value or issuance-by-kid breakdown exists (F23).

Assumption: the flat 36% step (rather than a near-100% failure) mildly argues against the simplest uniform parser break, and no log-level signature is available to confirm which validation step fails (log pipeline down).

Assumption: no earlier auth-service deploy or unqueried shared-component change (cache/DB/key store/secret store) contributed — the two-week auth-service deploy query returned budget_exhausted and redis-cache/user-db were never queried for changes.
Assumption: the 36% error rate reflects genuinely valid tokens being rejected (invalid_token on otherwise-valid requests) as described in the incident report, not a change in traffic mix.

timeline.event: market-data-service v5.0.3 deployed ('Fix symbol mapping'); the only other deployment in the 00:00-15:59Z window and not coincident with onset.
Last fully normal period: auth-service error_rate ~0.2%, request_rate ~391-409 req/s, p99 ~90ms; api-gateway 5xx ~0.2%.
auth-service error_rate bucket avg 0.23% — last clean 2-minute bucket.
Deployment dep-5710 of auth-service v7.3.0 goes live: 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten'; not rolled back (H1 trigger).
Config change cfg-2705 on auth-service by security-automation: jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' -> 'k-2026-04' ('Scheduled signing-key rotation') (H2 trigger).
auth-service error_rate step begins inside this bucket: avg 18.12%, max 36.08%.
auth-service error_rate reaches ~37.21% (max 38.34) in the first elevated 2-minute bucket; onset time is not separable from the 14:00Z deploy vs 14:01Z rotation.
Step fully established: auth-service error_rate avg 37.28%; api-gateway 5xx avg 21.21%, matching auth's onset bucket.

redis-cache healthy across onset: hit_ratio 96.0-96.2%, connected_clients ~304-320, evictions ~2.5-3.7/min flat; siblings portfolio-service/pricing-engine/market-data-service flat ~0.2%; order-service flat ~0.21% — no shared-component co-degradation.
auth-service still at ~36.31% (flat ~36% for ~2h, no recovery); api-gateway still ~21%.
Latest data point; no deploy or config change and no rollback occurred after onset.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0 -> previous version) as the single reversible auth-service change with an existing runbook precedent (HIST-109: 'Rolled back; pinned skew config'), and simultaneously re-publish/restore the previous signing key k-2025-10 alongside k-2026-04 rather than dropping it.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both candidate triggers (dep-5710 jjwt 0.12 parser rewrite and cfg-2705 key rotation from k-2025-10) are live and unrolled; reverting both is the safe mitigation when the two cannot be separated, and each has a matching historical precedent (HIST-109 for the library upgrade, HIST-108 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation' for the key change).

recommended_actions.action: If a single toggle must be tried first (smallest blast radius, no restart), restore the old key id k-2025-10 to resolvable/published state first — do not change the deploy yet; measure auth-service error_rate at 2-minute resolution for 10 minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2705 is one config value and reversible in seconds, and H2's failure mode is a resolvability problem for old-key tokens; a fast resolution of k-2025-10 would immediately show whether the ~36% step clears (H2) or persists (H1).

recommended_actions.action: If the key restore does not clear the errors, roll back dep-5710 and confirm whether the error rate returns to ~0.2% baseline within 2-4 minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: A parser-API change is a deployment-level revert; clearing on rollback distinguishes H1 from H2 and restores service immediately in either case.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument and capture the discriminating evidence that is currently missing: per-kid / per-issuer / per-audience / per-endpoint 401 counters on auth-service, and a pod-level version + loaded-key-id distribution (e.g. an endpoint or log line reporting loaded kid), plus JWKS publish/last-loaded timestamps and the token TTL/overlap/grace configuration.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are exactly the discriminators between H1 and H2 that are unavailable today (no per-kid/per-endpoint metric, no per-replica breakdown, no JWKS publish state or TTL config), and without them the same ambiguity will recur.

recommended_actions.action: Restore the identity-namespace log pipeline (separate ticket) and keep auth-service 401/validation-failure logs searchable, including kid/claim rejection reasons.
recommended_actions.rationale: Log retrieval for auth-service failed with 503 throughout the incident, blocking the only path to a token-class breakdown that would have discriminated H1 from H2.

recommended_actions.action: Add a pre-rotation key-overlap/grace window plus staged JWKS propagation with a verification gate before the old key is retired, and publish a per-pod 'JWKS loaded, key ids active' readiness signal.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-108 documents exactly this failure mode ('Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS'), and today there is no companion grace/overlap or JWKS publish config for auth-service (cfg-2705 is the only config entry), so the gap is structural.

recommended_actions.action: Add a canary/staged rollout policy for auth-service with per-replica error-rate alerting on any deploy touching the token-validation path, and enforce clock-skew configuration pinning as a guard for JWT-library upgrades.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-109 shows the same service regressed on a JWT-library upgrade via changed clock-skew default; per-replica metrics do not currently exist for auth-service, so a partial rollout cannot be detected today.

recommended_actions.action: While the discriminator instrumentation is absent, monitor redis-cache hit_ratio/evictions/connected_clients and sibling consumer error rates as a routine guard against shared-component hypotheses; today they are flat (~96% hit ratio, ~0.2% sibling error rates), so do not spend mitigation effort there.
recommended_actions.rationale: H3 (shared redis-cache fault) is contradicted by current telemetry, but this is the only shared component in auth-service's graph and the check is cheap and reusable.

data_gaps: No per-kid/issuer/audience or per-endpoint breakdown of the ~36% invalid_token 401s exists or was retrievable (available auth-service metrics are aggregate only; error_rate_by_kid and error_rate_by_endpoint both returned 'has no metric'), so the failing population cannot be matched to a token class.

No pod/instance-level or version/build label metrics exist for auth-service, so partial rollout of v7.3.0 versus a token-class subset cannot be distinguished; restarts are flat at 0, which neither shows nor excludes a subset of stale replicas.

auth-service logs were unretrievable throughout (query_logs returned 'backend unavailable (503)'), so no log-level error signature (which validation step, key id, audience) could corroborate either hypothesis.

No tool returns JWKS/key-store publish state, key last-loaded or publish timestamps, or token TTL/overlap/grace configuration, and the dependency graph contains no key-store/JWKS node — so whether k-2025-10 still resolves after 14:01Z (H2's pivotal hop) and what fraction of in-flight tokens carry it are undetermined.
The auth-service deployment query for 2026-04-01–2026-04-15 returned budget_exhausted, so any earlier auth-service deploy that could bear on validation behaviour is unverified.

redis-cache and user-db were never queried for deployments/config changes (only api-gateway was checked back to 2026-04-14), and nothing was queried before 2026-04-14, so a change to a shared component or an earlier secret-store change could exist outside the queried windows.

redis-cache exposes no error_rate/request_rate metric and its cpu_pct/memory_pct for 13:00-14:30Z were not executed (budget_exhausted); sibling-service latency was also not executed — though hit ratio, clients and evictions were verified flat.
Rollout/apply scope of cfg-2705 is known only at service granularity; no per-pod/per-instance config-apply telemetry exists to confirm atomic fleet-wide application versus propagation lag.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A per-kid or per-issuer breakdown of the failing 401s showing failures concentrated on tokens carrying k-2025-10 would confirm H2 (key rotation) and exonerate dep-5710.
A per-replica/version breakdown showing failures clustered on v7.3.0 replicas, or a rollback of dep-5710 clearing the error rate, would confirm H1 (bad deployment).
Evidence that k-2025-10 still resolves and is published after 14:01Z (JWKS publish state / key last-loaded timestamp) would refute H2's pivotal hop and shift the conclusion to H1.

Any additional deploy or config change on auth-service or a shared component (cache, DB, key store, secret store) within the 13:30-14:30Z window, or an auth-service deploy earlier in the two-week window, would reopen the origin question.
Auth-service logs showing the specific validation error (parser/claim rejection vs unresolved key id) would directly discriminate H1 from H2.
Restoring cfg-2705 to k-2025-10 without touching dep-5710 and observing the error rate clear (H2) or persist (H1) would be decisive.
Evidence that redis-cache or another shared component degraded at 14:02Z (e.g. connection errors) or that sibling consumers co-degraded would revive H3, though current telemetry contradicts this.

Findings that the 401s are actually generated by a client-side or caller/audience subset with no auth-side cause would revive H4, but the matched onset at auth-service and flat order-service make this unlikely.

findings.statement: Two deployments occurred across ALL services in 2026-04-15T00:00Z–15:59Z: market-data-service v5.0.3 at 11:35:00Z ("Fix symbol mapping"), and auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z ("Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation") whose changes are 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'. Neither was rolled back (rolled_back_at: null).

Exactly one config change occurred across all services in the window: cfg-2705 on auth-service, key 'jwt.signing.key_id' changed from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z by security-automation, described as 'Scheduled signing-key rotation' — i.e. one minute after the v7.3.0 deploy.

auth-service dependency graph: callers = api-gateway (http -> auth-service); callees = user-db (db), redis-cache (cache), kyc-provider (external). api-gateway is NOT marked shared, user-db is NOT marked shared; redis-cache IS marked shared=true with owner platform.

redis-cache is the shared component that auth-service uses and that several other services also use: auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service all have cache edges to redis-cache in the same graph.

api-gateway is the single front door for all listed services (downstream edges to auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, market-data-service, payment-service) and had NO deployments and NO config changes in 2026-04-14T00:00Z–15:59Z (both queries returned count 0) — so any gateway-side change would have to predate 2026-04-14.

Historical precedent: two prior incidents match '401 invalid_token' — HIST-109 (2025-07-11, 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', auth-service, root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default', fix: 'Rolled back; pinned skew config', match_score 5) and HIST-108 (2025-10-01, '401s after JWT signing key rotation', auth-service, symptoms '401 invalid_token / users logged out', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', category config_change, match_score 2). Both are leads only, not evidence about the current incident.

findings.statement: auth-service error_rate transitions from ~0.2% baseline to ~36-37% at 14:02Z: last normal 120s bucket is 14:00:00Z avg 0.21%, and the very next bucket 14:02:00Z is avg 37.21% (max 38.34). The change is effectively instantaneous at 2-minute resolution.

The 36% error rate is a sustained STEP, not a ramp or intermittent blip: at coarse 8-min buckets error_rate is ~0.2% through 13:52Z, then 36.27/35.79/35.98/36.55/36.01/35.67/35.96/36.6/35.9/36.3/36.29/36.47/35.55/36.31% from 14:08Z to 15:52Z, i.e. flat ~36% for ~2 hours with no recovery.

auth-service throughput and latency are UNCHANGED across the onset: request_rate is flat ~395-410 req/s throughout (12:00Z avg 391.27 to 15:52Z avg 409.06), and latency_p99_ms stays ~87-92ms on both sides of 14:00Z (13:52Z avg 90.7, 14:02Z-adjacent 14:00Z avg 89.67). No traffic surge or slowdown accompanies the 401s.

auth-service shows NO resource saturation coincident with onset: cpu_pct flat ~37-39% (14:00Z avg 38.69, 14:20Z avg 38.36), memory_pct flat ~51-53% (14:00Z avg 51.71), and rate_limited_per_min flat ~2/min (14:00Z avg 2.06) across 12:00-15:59Z. So the failure is not caused by CPU/memory pressure or rate limiting inside auth-service.

api-gateway (upstream caller of auth-service) shows a simultaneous step in HTTP 5xx error rate: ~0.2% baseline through 13:45Z (avg 0.24), jumping to avg 18.36% at the 14:00:00Z 15-min bucket and settling at ~21% (14:15Z avg 20.97, 15:45Z avg 21.02), i.e. ~21% sustained 5xx. This is a smaller fraction than auth's 36%, consistent with only the auth-calling subset of gateway traffic failing, but the onset bucket matches auth's 14:00-14:02Z onset.

Because auth-service error_rate rises to ~36% while its own request_rate stays constant (~399 req/s) and p99 latency is flat, the 401s are produced without any capacity/latency stress in auth-service itself — the failure is being returned quickly (invalid token), not timing out.

The entire change set bracketing the 14:02Z onset is two auth-service changes one minute apart: deployment dep-5710 auth-service v7.3.0 at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z ('jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten', status live, rolled_back_at null) and config cfg-2705 jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' -> 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z. No other deploys or config changes were found in 13:30–14:30Z, and both queries for 14:02–15:59Z returned count 0, so nothing was changed or rolled back after onset.

Onset timing is consistent with BOTH auth-service candidates and distinguishes neither: the last clean signal is 14:00Z, the deploy is at 14:00:00Z and the key rotation at 14:01:00Z, and T1 puts the first elevated error bucket at 14:02Z. The 2-minute bucket resolution cannot separate the two events, so timing alone cannot rule out either.

redis-cache is the only SHARED component in auth-service's dependency graph: it is marked shared=true/owner platform, and has cache edges from auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service. auth-service's other callees are user-db (shared=false) and kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry=false), and its sole caller api-gateway is shared=false. So a rotation/JWKS store or cache shared-component fault would have to route through redis-cache or the key store.

api-gateway is RULED OUT as the origin of the change: it is not shared, had zero deployments and zero config changes in 2026-04-14T00:00Z–15:59Z, and the only change set in the incident window is on auth-service. Its simultaneous ~21% 5xx step is therefore best explained as the auth-calling subset of its traffic failing, not a gateway-side change.

The ~1/3 (not all) failure pattern is more consistent with cfg-2705 key rotation than a full deploy: rotating the active signing key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 affects only tokens minted with the old key (those still within TTL / issued before rotation) while tokens already using the new key validate fine — a subset, time-decaying pattern. A clean library refactor would more typically break validation uniformly or for all audiences at once.

findings.statement: Prior precedents on this exact service/symptom split the two candidates: HIST-109 (2025-07-11, 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default', fix 'Rolled back; pinned skew config') mirrors dep-5710's JWT-library upgrade, while HIST-108 (2025-10-01, '401s after JWT signing key rotation', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', resolution 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation') mirrors cfg-2705. Both are leads only, but they show both candidates have a real precedent, so neither is exonerated by history.

cfg-2705 is recorded with scope = the whole auth-service ('scope':'auth-service'), not a pod/instance subset: the change is listed once for service 'auth-service' on key 'jwt.signing.key_id', and the same query run for all services returns count 1 with the same single entry. Nothing in the record indicates a canary/partial rollout — no per-pod or per-instance field or count exists.
findings.verification_note: 1/2 refs verified (tc-028: quote not found in tool output)

findings.statement: Across a two-week lookback (2026-04-01T00:00Z–2026-04-15T16:00Z) for auth-service, cfg-2705 is the ONLY config change recorded — count 1, single entry. There is no companion config entry for a key store, JWKS publish, key TTL, overlap, or grace-period setting anywhere on this service.

auth-service's full direct dependency picture (callers/callees, depth 2, downstream) contains no key store / JWKS service node: callees are user-db (postgres, shared=false), redis-cache (redis, shared=true), kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry=false). There is no signing-key store, secret manager, or JWKS endpoint represented, so any publish/last-loaded state would have to live outside the queryable dependency graph.

A targeted history search for JWKS/key-store publish behaviour ('old key retained', 'key store publish timestamp', 'last-loaded') returned only HIST-108, which asserts the mechanism 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS' with resolution 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation' — a lead (match_score 5), not evidence about the current incident; no historical record supplies an actual publish-state or TTL data series.

findings.statement: No evidence was obtainable to arbitrate H1 vs H2: the tool surface exposes no JWKS/key-store publish state, no key last-loaded or publish timestamp series, and no token TTL/overlap/grace configuration. The only change-set facts available remain cfg-2705 (14:01Z, service-scoped) and dep-5710 (14:00:00Z). Consequently whether old key k-2025-10 still resolves after 14:01Z — the pivotal hop for H2 — is undetermined, and the ~1/3 (vs ~36% error rate) fraction cannot be reconciled against a token-TTL population because no TTL value is retrievable.

redis-cache exposes NO error_rate or request_rate metric; its full available metric set is ['connected_clients','cpu_pct','evictions_per_min','hit_ratio_pct','memory_pct'] — so a cache-side error rate or connection-error counter cannot be measured directly.

redis-cache hit_ratio_pct is flat and healthy across the onset window: 96.01% at 13:48Z, 96.17% at 14:00Z, 96.02% at 14:06Z, 96.13% at 14:12Z, 95.7% at 14:18Z (range over 13:00–14:30Z 94.23–97.7, mean 95.94). No cache-effectiveness degradation at or after 14:02Z.

redis-cache connection load and eviction pressure are unchanged across onset: connected_clients ~304–320 through 13:00–14:30Z (13:54Z avg 306.8; 14:00Z avg 310.51; 14:06Z avg 308.05; 14:18Z avg 302.39), and evictions_per_min flat ~2.5–3.7 keys/min (13:54Z 3.02; 14:00Z 3.26; 14:06Z 3.72; 14:18Z 2.46). No connection storm and no eviction spike at 14:02Z.

portfolio-service error_rate shows NO change in the incident window: flat ~0.2% (max 0.32) in every 6-min bucket from 13:45Z (0.2) through 15:57Z (0.22), with 14:03Z avg 0.19 and 14:09Z avg 0.2 — i.e. no step at 14:02Z. Summary mean 0.21, missing_points 0.

pricing-engine and market-data-service error_rate likewise stay flat ~0.2% (max 0.32) across 13:45–15:59Z with no onset at 14:02Z: pricing-engine 14:03Z avg 0.23, 14:09Z avg 0.22, mean 0.22; market-data-service 14:03Z avg 0.21, 14:09Z avg 0.26, mean 0.21. Every sibling consumer of redis-cache remains healthy while auth-service sits at ~36%.

Co-degradation of the other redis-cache consumers is ABSENT: with redis-cache itself showing no fault metric and all three sibling consumers (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) flat at ~0.2% error rate 13:45–15:59Z, H3 (shared redis-cache fault) is not supported by the data and can be demoted to a documented assumption.

auth-service exposes NO per-endpoint, per-caller, per-issuer/audience or per-token-kid (kid/header) metric series. Querying error_rate for auth-service returned available_metrics = [cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts], and explicit queries for 'error_rate_by_kid' and 'error_rate_by_endpoint' both failed with 'has no metric', listing the same seven aggregate series. So no per-subset metric exists to attribute the ~36% invalid_token to a token class or caller.

No pod/instance-level (per-replica) breakdown exists for auth-service either: the metric list contains only aggregate series and there is no replica/version/build label dimension. Consequently the partial-rollout reading of H1 cannot be tested from metrics — failures cannot be shown to cluster on a subset of replicas.

auth-service pod restarts are flat at 0 across the whole window (12:00Z-15:30Z, cumulative), so the 14:02Z step is not accompanied by pod churn/restarts — no evidence of a crashing/cold-starting replica subset.

auth-service error_rate step at 2-minute resolution: 13:59Z avg 0.23%, then the 14:01:00Z bucket is avg 18.12% (max 36.08) and 14:03:00Z avg 37.28% (max 38.34) — i.e. the step begins inside the 14:01Z bucket and is fully established by 14:03Z, straddling the 14:00Z deploy and 14:01Z key rotation.

api-gateway 5xx mirrors auth's onset and is sustained at ~21%: 13:45Z bucket avg 0.25%, the next 540s bucket (13:54Z) avg 2.51% (max 20.72), then 14:03Z avg 21.21% steady through 15:51Z avg 20.71%. Its onset bucket matches auth's, but the ~21% level is smaller than auth's ~36%.

order-service (a sibling behind the same api-gateway front door) shows a completely flat error_rate of ~0.21% across 13:45Z-15:40Z (every bucket avg 0.19-0.21, max 0.31-0.32) — no step at 14:02Z. This shows the gateway's 5xx step is confined to traffic that calls auth-service, not a gateway-wide/global fault, ruling out other gateway downstreams as the source.
